root_cause.text: XFS attribute leaf freemap maintenance could leave a zero-length freemap entry with a nonzero base, so later `_remove`/`_add` logic that matches freemap entries by base could create overlapping or duplicate freemap records and misplace new xattr data over the entries array in `xfs_attr3_leaf_add_work()`.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds a check in `fs/xfs/libxfs/xfs_attr_leaf.c` to zero `freemap[i].base` when `freemap[i].size == 0`, with the comment explicitly stating that zero-length freemaps with nonzero base confuse `_remove` and can create overlapping freemaps; the CVE text further says this can lead to two entries with the same base and a subsequent `_leaf_add` allocating xattr name/value entries on top of the entries array, causing data loss.

intent_record.intent_summary: Clear invalid zero-length freemap entries to prevent overlapping freemap corruption in XFS attribute leaf handling.
intent_record.what: The patch adds a new conditional inside xfs_attr3_leaf_add_work() that checks each freemap entry after its size has been adjusted; if an entry has size 0 and a nonzero base, it resets base to 0 and sets ichdr->holes to 1. A comment is added explaining that zero-length freemaps with nonzero base should not be left behind because they can confuse _remove() and lead to overlapping freemaps.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this prevents stale freemap records from retaining a valid-looking base address when they no longer describe usable space. That avoids later freemap removal logic from matching on an obsolete base and mistakenly creating overlapping freemap regions. If all freemap entries are effectively removed, the next add path will compact the leaf block and rebuild the freemap state.

candidates.rationale: This insertion point is where the leaf bookkeeping proceeds after freemap processing; if a zero-length freemap entry with a nonzero base is left uncleared, later add/remove matching can mis-handle space accounting and place new xattr data over the entries array.

vuln_statements.explanation: This bookkeeping statement executes after freemap processing in xfs_attr3_leaf_add_work(). If a zero-length freemap entry with a nonzero base is left uncleared, later freemap matching by base can create overlapping or duplicate records, causing new xattr data to be placed over the entries array.

bic_trace_step.reason: The shown function `xfs_attr3_leaf_add_work()` only updates freemap entries by matching the exact base at the old end of the entry array: `if (ichdr->freemap[i].base == tmp) { ichdr->freemap[i].base += sizeof(xfs_attr_leaf_entry_t); ichdr->freemap[i].size -= sizeof(xfs_attr_leaf_entry_t); }`. There is no logic here that creates, removes, or repairs a zero-length freemap entry with a nonzero base, nor any handling of overlapping/duplicate freemap records. The vulnerable construct described in the root cause is therefore not present in this snippet, and the fix for that specific condition is also absent.
